lessons.title: Review — the three se's
lessons.gloss: review — the three se's, two of which are one word and one of which is an impostor

segments.text: Nothing new. Say se llama, then se habla español, then se lo digo. Three sentences, three ses, learned about a hundred chapters apart.

utterances: reflexive. example: se llama. what the se is: himself.
impersonal. example: se habla español. what the se is: nobody named.
the impostor. example: se lo digo. what the se is: le, in disguise.

segments.text: And here is the fact that makes this a review rather than a fourth thing to learn:
The first two are the same word. The third is not.
The impersonal grew out of the reflexive — the books sell themselves becoming books are sold — which is why the verb still agrees with the thing. Same word, stretched.
The third only looks like them. It is Latin illī — the le you already know — which arrived at this spelling by an accident of medieval pronunciation, as you saw when gelo became se lo.
So Spanish does not have three ses. It has two, and a coincidence.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: how to tell them apart in the wild

segments.text: You will not have to work this out consciously for long, but while you do:
Is there a lo, la, los or las right after it? Then it is the impostor: se lo, se la. It means to him / to her / to them.
Otherwise, is anybody named as the doer? If not, it is the impersonal: se habla, se dice, se come bien.
Otherwise it is the reflexive, pointing back at whoever the sentence is about: se llama, se levanta.
The first test is nearly free, because that direct object pronoun is sitting right there in the open.

segments.instruction: "se llama", "se habla español", "se lo digo" — two of these are relatives
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "se llama", "se habla español", "se lo digo" — two of these are relatives]

segments.prompt: Of the three se's, which two are really one word?

feedback.correct: The impersonal grew out of the reflexive.
feedback.incorrect: The reflexive and the impersonal. The se of se lo is a different word entirely.

segments.prompt: What single thing right after se tells you it is the impostor?

feedback.correct: Sitting right there in the open.
feedback.incorrect: A lo, la, los or las immediately after it.

segments.prompt: Which se is in como se dice?

feedback.correct: Asking how it gets said, not who says it.
feedback.incorrect: The impersonal. Nobody is named as the sayer.

segments.text: How many ses does Spanish really have? (Two, and a coincidence.) Which one is the impostor? (The one in se lo — it is le.) Next: all of it in a place you would actually meet it.
